card.name: Election and voting words in civic text
card.fires_on: Words that sit right where an election or ballot idea is expected, such as elected, for (office), on (issues), or a space after a proposition number. Seen in political and government text.

modes.label: Elected / office-holding verbs
modes.description: The word elected or a nearby word about holding or leaving office in descriptions of governments.
modes.example: President Armando Guebuza was<< elected>> in December 2004 in

modes.label: Linking words in voting phrases
modes.description: Small words like for or on that follow voters, candidates, or ballot measures.
modes.example: The political season is heating up, and once again the statewide ballot includes several measures that ask voters to weigh in<< on>> important state policy issues.

modes.label: After ballot proposition numbers
modes.description: The space after a proposition number, just before the next number in a list.
modes.example: To help voters better understand Propositions 30 and<< >>38, a new CBP analysis
